questions.explanation: Moist dirty bedding creates conditions where disease-causing germs can grow.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze housing conditions that affect the health of small domestic animals.

questions.prompt: A menu has ugali, rice, and chapati only. What is the main weakness of this menu?
options: It lacks enough body-building and protective foods
It has too many fruits
It contains no energy foods
It has too much clean water
questions.correctAnswer: It lacks enough body-building and protective foods
questions.explanation: The menu is mainly energy foods and should include protein, vegetables, or fruits.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze a meal and identify missing food groups.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to cook sukuma wiki with little nutrient loss. Which choice is best?
options: Wash before cutting and cook for a short time
Cut first, soak overnight, then overcook
Boil for one hour and pour away all water
Leave it uncovered in dust before cooking
questions.correctAnswer: Wash before cutting and cook for a short time
questions.explanation: Washing before cutting and short cooking help reduce nutrient loss and contamination.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze food preparation choices that conserve nutrients.

questions.prompt: A seedbed has many seedlings close together and some are yellowing. Which reason is most likely?
options: The seedlings are competing for light, water, and nutrients
The seedlings have too much space
The soil has changed into plastic
The seedlings no longer need roots
questions.correctAnswer: The seedlings are competing for light, water, and nutrients
questions.explanation: Overcrowded seedlings compete and may become weak, so thinning may be needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze signs that show a seedbed needs thinning or better care.

questions.prompt: A packet of flour is torn but the expiry date has not passed. What should a learner consider before using it?
options: It may be contaminated because the package is open
It is always safer than sealed flour
The torn packet adds nutrients
The date no longer matters for any food
questions.correctAnswer: It may be contaminated because the package is open
questions.explanation: A damaged package can allow dirt, pests, or moisture into food even before the expiry date.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze package condition and date information when judging food safety.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains why dried foods should cool before being packed in containers?
options: Warm food may produce moisture that encourages spoilage
Cooling changes food into plastic
Warm food cannot fit into containers
Cooling removes every nutrient
questions.correctAnswer: Warm food may produce moisture that encourages spoilage
questions.explanation: Packing warm dried food can trap moisture, making mould growth more likely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain storage steps that keep preserved foods safe.

questions.prompt: A school has limited money for lunch ingredients. Which choice gives the best value for a balanced meal?
options: Maize, beans, cabbage, and seasonal fruit
Soda, sweets, and crisps
Only white bread for every learner
Sugar, salt, and cooking oil only
questions.correctAnswer: Maize, beans, cabbage, and seasonal fruit
questions.explanation: Local staples, pulses, vegetables, and seasonal fruit can provide a balanced meal at lower cost.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate affordable local food choices for balanced meals.

questions.prompt: A class compost pit is close to a water tap and gives a bad smell. What is the best conclusion?
options: The site may be unsuitable and the pit needs better management
The smell proves the tap is cleaner
Compost should always be placed beside drinking water
The class should add plastic bottles to stop smell
questions.correctAnswer: The site may be unsuitable and the pit needs better management
questions.explanation: Compost should be placed safely and managed with suitable materials, moisture, and covering.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze hygiene problems linked to organic waste management.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best shows that a rabbit feeding plan is working well?
options: Rabbits are active, growing, and finishing clean feed
Rabbits are losing weight and feed is mouldy
Water containers are always empty and dirty
The hutch has no ventilation
questions.correctAnswer: Rabbits are active, growing, and finishing clean feed
questions.explanation: Healthy behaviour, growth, and clean feeding show that the feeding plan is suitable.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate signs of effective feeding and care in small animals.

questions.prompt: Which reason best explains why raw and cooked foods should be kept separate?
options: Germs from raw food can move to cooked food
Cooked food becomes raw again when covered
Raw food always improves cooked food
Separate storage removes all nutrients
questions.correctAnswer: Germs from raw food can move to cooked food
questions.explanation: Cooked food is ready to eat, so it should be protected from germs on raw food.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how cross-contamination happens during food handling.

questions.prompt: A group keeps watering a seedbed until puddles form. What is the likely effect?
options: Seedlings may rot or be washed away
The seedbed will need no care forever
All weeds will disappear permanently
The soil will become dry immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Seedlings may rot or be washed away
questions.explanation: Too much water can damage roots, encourage disease, and move soil or seedlings.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the effects of overwatering a seedbed.

questions.prompt: Which option best explains why crop rotation can help a vegetable garden?
options: It can reduce repeated pest problems and support soil fertility
It makes all crops grow without water
It changes weeds into vegetables
It stops learners from needing tools
questions.correctAnswer: It can reduce repeated pest problems and support soil fertility
questions.explanation: Changing crops in a bed can break pest cycles and use soil nutrients more wisely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how crop rotation supports healthy vegetable production.

questions.prompt: A learner compares boiled eggs and bean stew as protein foods. What is a fair conclusion?
options: Both can help build and repair the body
Only eggs contain any useful nutrient
Beans are not food because they grow in soil
Both foods are mainly drinking water
questions.correctAnswer: Both can help build and repair the body
questions.explanation: Eggs and beans are protein foods, though they come from different sources.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare plant and animal sources of protein.

questions.prompt: Which observation best shows that soil erosion is beginning on a path beside a garden?
options: Small channels are forming where water flows
Leaves are green after watering
Mulch is covering the soil well
The path is protected by grass
questions.correctAnswer: Small channels are forming where water flows
questions.explanation: Small channels show runoff is cutting into the soil and may become larger if not controlled.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize early signs of erosion and explain their meaning.

questions.prompt: A kitchen has clean water, soap, bins with lids, and a raised dish rack. What can you conclude?
options: The kitchen supports good hygiene practices
The kitchen cannot be used safely
The bins make handwashing unnecessary
The dish rack makes food spoil faster
questions.correctAnswer: The kitchen supports good hygiene practices
questions.explanation: Clean water, soap, covered bins, and raised drying areas help prevent contamination.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate kitchen features that support hygienic food preparation.

questions.prompt: Why might a learner choose boiling instead of deep frying for a child recovering from illness?
options: Boiled food can be softer and use less fat
Deep frying removes all germs from hands
Boiling makes food impossible to digest
Deep frying always adds vitamins
questions.correctAnswer: Boiled food can be softer and use less fat
questions.explanation: Soft foods with less fat can be easier to eat and digest during recovery.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose cooking methods for different nutrition and health needs.

questions.prompt: A farm near a school has runoff carrying soil into a drainage channel. Which solution treats the cause best?
options: Plant cover crops and guide water along contours
Sweep the soil farther into the drain
Remove all plants from the land
Dig deeper channels straight downhill
questions.correctAnswer: Plant cover crops and guide water along contours
questions.explanation: Cover crops protect soil, and contour guidance slows water instead of increasing erosion.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate methods for reducing runoff and soil loss on sloping land.

questions.prompt: A class has a dry week, a small water supply, and a vegetable nursery. Which plan is best?
options: Water early, mulch the beds, shade lightly, and check soil moisture daily
Water at noon only and remove all mulch
Flood the nursery once and ignore it
Stop checking the nursery until the dry week ends
questions.correctAnswer: Water early, mulch the beds, shade lightly, and check soil moisture daily
questions.explanation: The plan combines timing, mulching, light shade, and monitoring to conserve water while protecting seedlings.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a practical water-conservation plan for a vegetable nursery.

questions.prompt: A school wants to rear rabbits for a club project. Which plan is most complete?
options: Build a ventilated hutch, provide clean feed and water, keep records, and clean regularly
Buy rabbits and keep them in a wet box without records
Feed rabbits only on market waste without checking freshness
Let rabbits roam near the road every day
questions.correctAnswer: Build a ventilated hutch, provide clean feed and water, keep records, and clean regularly
questions.explanation: Successful rabbit rearing needs suitable housing, feeding, hygiene, and records.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan key requirements for a small domestic animal project.

questions.prompt: A learner must prepare a balanced supper using ugali, omena, cowpeas leaves, and oranges. Which explanation best justifies the meal?
options: It has energy food, protein food, vegetables, and fruit
It has only energy foods
It lacks any protective foods
It is balanced only because it has ugali
questions.correctAnswer: It has energy food, protein food, vegetables, and fruit
questions.explanation: Ugali gives energy, omena gives protein and minerals, cowpeas leaves and oranges add protective nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Justify a balanced meal plan using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: A garden borders a wildlife path. Which plan protects crops while respecting wild animals?
options: Use fencing, scare devices, and harvest ripe crops on time
Block the wildlife path with harmful traps
Leave all crops exposed and then chase animals at night
Destroy the nearby habitat to move animals away
questions.correctAnswer: Use fencing, scare devices, and harvest ripe crops on time
questions.explanation: Physical barriers, scare devices, and timely harvesting reduce crop damage without harming wildlife.
questions.learningOutcome: Design humane crop-protection strategies near wildlife areas.

questions.prompt: A family stores maize in sacks, but the store is damp and sacks touch the wall. Which improvement is best?
options: Dry the maize well, place sacks on pallets, and improve ventilation
Add wet grass between the sacks
Move sacks to the bathroom floor
Close all air spaces and keep the store dark
questions.correctAnswer: Dry the maize well, place sacks on pallets, and improve ventilation
questions.explanation: Dry grain, raised storage, and airflow reduce moisture, pests, and mould.
questions.learningOutcome: Recommend improvements for safe storage of cereals.

questions.prompt: A class wants to sell dried mango slices at a school event. Which plan best protects consumers?
options: Wash fruit, slice with clean tools, dry on raised covered trays, and pack in clean containers
Slice unwashed fruit on the floor and pack while wet
Dry mangoes beside rubbish and leave them uncovered
Mix fresh and mouldy slices to increase quantity
questions.correctAnswer: Wash fruit, slice with clean tools, dry on raised covered trays, and pack in clean containers
questions.explanation: Clean preparation, protected drying, and clean packaging keep dried fruit safer for consumers.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a hygienic process for preserving fruit by drying.

questions.prompt: A vegetable bed has poor growth, many weeds, and dry soil. Which plan addresses all three problems?
options: Weed the bed, add compost, water near roots, and mulch
Add more weeds and stop watering
Remove crops and leave the soil bare
Water the path and ignore the crop roots
questions.correctAnswer: Weed the bed, add compost, water near roots, and mulch
questions.explanation: Weeding reduces competition, compost improves fertility, and watering with mulch conserves moisture.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a care plan for improving vegetable crop growth.

questions.prompt: A school kitchen wants to reduce food-borne illness. Which routine is most complete?
options: Wash hands, clean surfaces, separate raw and cooked foods, cook well, and cover food
Only sweep the floor once a week
Taste all food with the same unwashed spoon
Store cooked food uncovered near waste bins
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands, clean surfaces, separate raw and cooked foods, cook well, and cover food
questions.explanation: Food safety needs clean hands and surfaces, separation, proper cooking, and protection after cooking.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a routine for safe food handling in a school kitchen.

questions.prompt: A group must choose between deep frying mandazi and steaming sweet potatoes for a healthy snack day. Which judgement is best?
options: Steamed sweet potatoes use less fat and keep the snack simple
Deep frying is always healthier because it uses more oil
Both snacks have no nutrients
Mandazi becomes fruit when fried
questions.correctAnswer: Steamed sweet potatoes use less fat and keep the snack simple
questions.explanation: Steaming uses little or no fat, while deep frying adds more oil to the snack.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate cooking methods when choosing healthier snacks.

questions.prompt: A school compound has food waste, stagnant water, and a dusty food preparation table. Which action plan is best?
options: Compost suitable waste, drain stagnant water, and clean the table before food work
Move waste beside the table and start cooking
Cover stagnant water with food sacks
Ignore the compound because cooking happens indoors
questions.correctAnswer: Compost suitable waste, drain stagnant water, and clean the table before food work
questions.explanation: The plan manages waste, removes a mosquito breeding place, and makes food preparation hygienic.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a practical hygiene plan for a school compound and food area.
